data.title: Lowe's partners with Bilt to expand loyalty rewards, AI-powered commerce
data.description:
Lowe’s Companies Inc. has partnered with housing rewards platform Bilt to expand its loyalty reach. The partnership lets Bilt members earn points on Lowe’s purchases and use those rewards toward a home maintenance subscription.

Announced Nov. 10, the tie-up makes Lowe’s Bilt’s exclusive home improvement partner, connecting the retailer with the platform’s more than 8 million members. The companies also plan to launch a curated Lowe’s marketplace within Bilt in early 2027.

“By partnering with Bilt, we can meet customers in a community they already know and love and connect them to Lowe’s products, services and rewards in a way that feels simple and seamless,” said Jen Wilson, Lowe’s executive vice president and chief marketing officer, in the company’s announcement.

The partnership runs on Bilt’s new Neighborhood OS. The artificial intelligence (AI)-powered commerce platform helps businesses reach nearby consumers with personalized offers and loyalty benefits.

Lowe’s ranks No. 9 in Digital Commerce 360’s Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales.

Lowe’s is No. 90 in Digital Commerce 360 and ReFiBuy’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

How Lowe’s and Bilt rewards work together

Bilt members can now earn rewards through both loyalty programs.

Its members can link an existing MyLowe’s Rewards account — or create one — to earn one Bilt Point per dollar on eligible Lowe’s purchases. Additionally, they can earn MyLowe’s Money through the retailer’s loyalty program. MyLowe’s Rewards benefits include free shipping and exclusive member deals.

The agreement adds Lowe’s to Bilt’s network of more than 50,000 merchant partners nationwide, including restaurants and fitness studios. Through Neighborhood OS, Lowe’s can reach members with offers and rewards based on where they live and direct them to nearby stores.

The partnership also gives members another way to pay for Lowe’s home maintenance services. Bilt members can use Bilt Points, Bilt Cash or a linked payment card to purchase a Lowe’s HomeCare+ subscription, the companies said.

The subscription costs $99 annually and includes two in-home visits by trained Lowe’s associates, covering up to seven maintenance services. Subscribers also receive 5% off products used during those services and Gold MyLowe’s Rewards benefits. HomeCare+ is available in select ZIP codes and renews each year automatically.

Bilt’s Neighborhood OS manages enrollment, checks service availability at members’ addresses and processes subscription payments, Lowe’s said. The companies plan to add matching with existing MyLowe’s Rewards accounts in December.

How Bilt Neighborhood OS uses AI to connect businesses and shoppers

Bilt’s Neighborhood OS connects with businesses’ existing payment, reservation and customer-management systems. This allows merchants to target nearby shoppers with offers, recognize returning customers and track spending tied to promotions.

“For example, a neighborhood restaurant can identify prospective customers, launch a targeted offer to bring them in, recognize them when they visit, and automatically apply the appropriate benefit through its existing point-of-sale system,” Bilt said in its announcement.

The platform also uses AI agents to manage tasks such as reservations, customer communications and marketing across those connected systems.

In the 30 days before its announcement, Bilt said its AI agents completed more than 2 million actions across more than 29,000 businesses, with 91% of those actions requiring no human intervention.

The platform builds on Bilt’s expansion beyond rent rewards. Founded in 2021, the company has added mortgage rewards, local shopping, travel and home services.

Bilt estimates that roughly $6.6 trillion in annual U.S. retail and food-services spending takes place in person. Its members generated more than $12 billion in rewarded commerce at local businesses over the past 12 months, the company said.

How loyalty rewards influence shopping behavior

Lowe’s brings an established loyalty program to the partnership. MyLowe’s Rewards had more than 30 million members, who shopped twice as often and spent more than 50% more than nonmembers, the retailer said in its 2025 annual report.

Bilt’s research points to consumers’ willingness to try nearby businesses that offer rewards. In its first-ever State of the Neighborhood 2026 study, 95% of respondents said they would try a local business at least once if they could earn points or rewards there. Another 87% said they would shop more frequently at a local business offering those incentives.

The study also found that two-thirds of Americans make at least 80% of their everyday spending within their neighborhoods, with the median consumer shopping within 15 miles of home. Conducted by 451 Research by S&P Global on Bilt’s behalf, the survey covered 6,591 U.S. adults in March and April 2026.

Bilt expands partnerships across retail, technology and services

data.title: eBay adds visual identification to listing generation options
data.description:
Ebay has been building out features for its seller-focused “magical listing tool” for years, and the latest options to debut include a workflow that takes a user directly from their own photo to an artificial intelligence (AI)-generated listing.

The online marketplace announced the new feature on Nov. 11, sharing that it would be available in Australia, France, Germany, Italy, the U.K., and the U.S.

EBay ranks No. 6 in Digital Commerce 360’s Global Online Marketplaces Database. The market research tool ranks the 100 largest such marketplaces by third-party gross merchandise value (GMV).

How does eBay’s new visual identification feature work?

The process for sellers to take photos of their items with their own cameras and use those photos to begin creating eBay listings consists of three steps, according to details published in a corporate blog post.

First, the seller needs to take a photo of their item and share it with eBay. Then, the magical listing tool uses AI to identify what’s in the photo and fill out the listing fields. According to eBay, at that point, all the seller needs to do is review their draft for corrections and then publish.

EBay noted that the process builds off of a mobile listing creation flow that it debuted in 2025.

What eBay has added to its magical listing tool over time

“Magical listing is streamlining listing creation and bringing more C2C inventory onto eBay, while AI enhancements to search and discovery are helping buyers more easily find the most relevant items across our 2.6 billion listings,” said eBay CEO Jamie Iannone during the company’s Q2 earnings call in August.

EBay noted in its Nov. 11 announcement that 10 million unique sellers have used AI features on eBay, resulting in 800,000 new listings daily.

“In Q2, we began integrating enhanced pricing guidance into magical listing to help sellers balance velocity and price realization, and we improved the accuracy of package size estimates to help manage shipping costs more efficiently,” Iannone stated.

He previously referenced a “new experience leverages AI agents from the start to autonomously build listings from images alone” in March.

The online marketplace shared more features in April, setting the stage for the latest updates, with options to generate listings from photos and titles. At the time, it noted that testing in the U.K. showed that the AI features “led to a 50% reduction in the total steps needed to list and faster listing times.”

data.title: The Children’s Place bankruptcy filing sets bidding in December
data.description:
The Children’s Place Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in a series of documents dated Nov. 8. The children’s apparel retailer announced its plans that same day, outlining that it would pursue the sale of “substantially all of its assets” and would begin accepting bids in December.

As the process moves forward, The Children’s Place expects to leave its ecommerce sites and physical stores open. However, it views its next steps as a means to fund a broad restructuring.

The Children’s Place is No. 199 in the Top 1000 Database. The database tracks North America’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

“Today’s announcement marks an important step in our efforts to secure the best path forward for The Children’s Place,” said Rudy Morando, co-chief restructuring officer of The Children’s Place. “For nearly 60 years, The Children’s Place has supported growing families with apparel that customers have come to know and love.”

Financial struggles at The Children’s Place have been ongoing. In the retailer’s fiscal second quarter ended Aug. 1, the company reported an 18.9% net sales decrease year over year to $241.8 million, leaving it with a $31.0 million loss.

In the meantime, U.S. Securities and Exchange filings on Nov. 4 showed that four high-level executives had departed. They included:

  • Muhammad Asif Seemab, interim CEO
  • Muhammad Umair, chief strategy officer
  • Turki Saleh AlRajhi, executive chair
  • Kim Roy, director

At the time, John Szczepanski was announced to be stepping in as acting president.

Next steps for The Children’s Place

“We recognize the significance of this development for our employees, customers, vendors, and other partners, and we are committed to conducting an efficient and transparent sale process,” said Morando. “In the meantime, we remain focused on serving the families who have trusted The Children’s Place for generations.”

In a press release, The Children’s Place laid out a December timeline for the sale of its assets. It expects parties to submit bids by Dec. 9. Subsequently, it anticipates that a court-supervised sale process will conclude by the end of 2026.

data.title: e.l.f. Beauty Q2 sales grow 51% as it embraces digital platforms
data.description:
E.l.f. Beauty Inc. raised its full-year outlook for the second straight quarter after net sales increased 51% in its fiscal Q2 2027, helped by Rhode’s launch at Sephora in Europe and a rebound in unit sales for the core e.l.f. brand.

Net sales for the quarter ended Sept. 30 reached $520.8 million, an increase from $343.9 million a year earlier. It was the company’s 31st consecutive quarter of net sales growth, CEO Tarang Amin said. 

E.l.f. said sales grew in both retailer and ecommerce channels in the U.S. and abroad.

Organic net sales rose about 35%, chief financial officer Mandy Fields said on the earnings call. Rhode, which e.l.f. acquired in August 2025, added about 16 percentage points to total growth in the month before the deal’s anniversary on Aug. 5.

E.l.f. Beauty ranks No. 328 in Digital Commerce 360’s Top 1000 Database, which ranks North America’s leading online retailers by annual web sales.

E.l.f. Beauty is also No. 327 in Digital Commerce 360 and ReFiBuy’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

Amazon and TikTok Shop drive digital sales

Connected commerce, which e.l.f. uses to describe sales through online platforms, accounted for 31% of sales in Q2, Amin said. 

In the U.S., e.l.f. was the top cosmetics brand on Amazon and the most-searched. On TikTok Shop, e.l.f. Cosmetics climbed to No. 2 in cosmetics.

Amazon ranks No. 3 in Digital Commerce 360’s Global Online Marketplaces Database. That database ranks the 100 largest such marketplaces by third-party gross merchandise value (GMV).

E.l.f. is also using digital platforms to test new categories. In October, the retailer launched e.l.f. Pop, a fragrance and body collection, exclusively on Amazon and TikTok Shop, with more scents planned later this fiscal year. E.l.f. Hair launched in July with a six-product assortment priced at $10 or less, exclusively at Target. It is already among Target’s top 20 hair care brands, Amin said, and about half its buyers are new to e.l.f.

Rhode’s direct-to-consumer site remains a strong channel alongside its retail expansion, Amin said. A limited-edition collection with influencer Alexandra Leclerc had a waitlist of more than 200,000 people and mostly sold out within an hour. E.l.f. has not seen higher customer acquisition costs for Rhode, he said.

Rhode’s European launch lifts international sales

Rhode launched at Sephora in 19 European countries in September. Amin said the launch marked “the biggest launch in Sephora’s history.” He also said Rhode is the top brand Sephora carries in Europe, with one of the strongest repeat rates the retailer sees. Rhode is still in only about 40% of Sephora locations worldwide, he said.

E.l.f. international net sales grew 165% in Q2, while U.S. net sales rose 25%. International sales accounted for about 25% of net sales on a trailing 12-month basis. In May, Digital Commerce 360 reported the figure was about 20%. Amin said legacy beauty peers generate about 70% of their sales abroad.

Fields said the core e.l.f. brand also improved in its largest international markets: Canada, the U.K. and Germany.

e.l.f. expects growth to slow in second half of 2027

E.l.f. now expects fiscal 2027 net sales growth of 22% to 24%, up from a projected 18% to 20% last quarter and 12% to 14% in May. 

The beauty retailer expects second-half net sales growth of about 7-10%, with Q3 above that range and Q4 below it. Fields tied the Q4 slowdown to last year’s launches, including e.l.f.’s expanded space at Ulta Beauty, its launch with dm in Germany, Rhode’s launch at MECCA in Australia and New Zealand and Naturium’s first expansion into Walmart.

Fields said the 7% to 10% growth outlook is well ahead of the beauty category, which is growing at a low-single-digit rate.

data.title: Under Armour Q2 sales slide as CEO cites optimism about AI
data.description:
Under Armour CEO Kevin Plank spoke in optimistic terms about the sports apparel and equipment brand’s road ahead, even as net revenue fell 6.9% year over year to $1.24 billion in the fiscal second quarter ended Sept. 30.

“We delivered against our revenue expectation and exceeded our operating income outlook,” said Plank in the company’s earnings announcement. “As we progress in this transformation, we are driving greater efficiency across our business, sharpening our product offering, and amplifying global marketing to strengthen our brand and improve financial performance.”

In the meantime, Under Armour shared that it incurred a total of $13 million in Q2 costs released to its Fiscal 2025 Restructuring Plan, which expects to be “substantially complete” by the end of 2026. It expects full fiscal year revenue to ultimately fall year over year “at a mid-single-digit percentage rate.”

Under Armour is No. 158 in the Top 1000 Database. The database tracks North America’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

Under Armour wholesale and ecommerce sales in Q2

“Wholesale revenue decreased 6% to $725 million, reflecting the impact of softer full-price sell-through and pressure in parts of the distributor business, partly offset by select accounts and markets,” Plank told investors on Under Armour’s Q2 earnings call. “Direct-to-consumer revenue decreased 8% to $494 million, including a 7% decline in owned and operated stores and a 12% decline in ecommerce.”

Plank attributed the drops to a reduction in overall traffic.

“Traffic remained the primary challenge, particularly in North America, with better conversion and targeted digital initiatives providing some offset,” he stated.

How Plank expects Under Armour to benefit from AI

Speaking to analysts on the Nov. 6 earnings call, Plank touched on the role he sees artificial intelligence (AI) playing as Under Armour seeks to complete a turnaround for its business.

“I think that our industry actually lines and maps up perfectly for the advantage of what AI brings for us,” he stated.

Primarily, he noted that he believes the company needs to focus on three areas to realize benefits from AI. Those include supply chain, merchandising and marketing.

Nevertheless, he cautioned that the answer to solving Under Armour’s problems would have to eventually address one topic: “ship us everything that we ordered.” In that context, he added that “accuracy and delivering on time and full is also a priority.”
